## Statements

- Stated by host (opencode-go-docs, Where can I use it?): Go routes and caches by session: identify the client with its own user agent and send a stable x-opencode-session per conversation, unless the client sends a native session header Go recognises.
- Stated by host (opencode-go-docs, Validated Clients): Go names Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, ZCode, Pi, jcode, and Kilo Code CLI as working clients. Hermes, jcode, and Kilo Code CLI need a build with the session-header fix.
- Stated by host (opencode-go-docs, Known Problematic Clients): Go reports incomplete session support for DeepSeek Harness, GitHub Copilot Chat, Kimi Code, and MiMo Code, so cache reuse and routing through them may be weaker.
- Stated by host (opencode-go-docs, Usage limits): Go caps each model by dollar spend: 20% of its monthly limit per 5 hours and 50% per week. Costlier models such as Kimi K3, Grok 4.7, and Qwen3.8 Max run out fastest; batch work accordingly.
- Stated by host (opencode-go-docs, Estimated requests, Kimi K3 row): Kimi K3 has one of the smallest monthly allowances on Go, about 490 requests a month at typical usage on the base plan. Save it for work that needs it.
- Stated by host (opencode-go-docs, Privacy, Grok 4.7/4.6 note): On Go, zero data retention for Grok 4.7 and 4.6 disables the stateful Responses API, Files and Collections, and the Batch API. Do not plan on those through this route.
- Stated by host (opencode-go-docs, Privacy, Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor note): The Muse Spark contributor route on Go is discounted because Meta may train on your prompts and completions, and it is limited to permitted regions. Send no private code through it.
- Stated by host (opencode-go-docs, Usage limits, GPT 6 Luna rows): GPT 6 Luna prices step up for requests above 272K tokens (input $0.10 to $0.20, output $0.50 to $0.75 per 1M), so keep prompts under that size.
- Stated by host (opencode-go-docs, Usage limits, Grok 4.7 and Grok 4.6 rows): Grok 4.7 and 4.6 cost double per token once a request passes 200K tokens on Go, so keep prompts under that size.
- Stated by host (opencode-go-docs, Usage limits, DeepSeek peak-hours note): DeepSeek V4.1 Flash costs double during peak hours on Go, 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC on weekdays. Schedule bulk work off-peak.
- Stated by host (opencode-go-docs, Usage limits, LongCat 2.5 Preview Free row): LongCat 2.5 Preview Free costs nothing on Go and has no usage cap, but only for a limited time. Do not build a standing route on it.
- Stated by host (opencode-go-docs, Estimated requests, Qwen3.8 Max row): Qwen3.8 Max has one of the smallest monthly allowances on Go, about 810 requests a month at typical usage on the base plan. Save it for work that needs it.
